title: How can I make Claude good at Blender?
author: Fluid_Equal_4942
selftext: How can I make Claude good at Blender? Like, really good, so it can finish the whole game without other AI API.

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: Give it some reference, use germini to create turn around character model sheets, ask him to make no mistakes

replies.author: sexual--predditor
replies.body:
> ask him to make no mistakes

Can't tell if joking or serious

replies.author: Bluetails_Buizel
replies.body: Joking, mistakes are allowed so that both bot and user learns from mistakes.

comments.author: work_guy
comments.body: Well it’s already as good at it as it’s able. The real answer is hours and hours of iteration. Tell Claude to have sub agents review all outputs as blind reviewers that have, as you’d define, your requirements. Then wait hours, spend lots and lots of tokens, and be prepared to realize that AI vision isn’t actually that great. Assuming you’re looking for an easy solution: there isn’t one. It’s the current gap in AI gamedev. Practical advice: lower your expectations and tailor your games art style to something forgiving to imperfection. Or simply things in a way that makes the shortcomings part of its style. They’re perfectly capable of that currently.

replies.author: Fit-Secretary2495
replies.body: It just sucks to compromise on an immersive 3d experience

replies.author: work_guy
replies.body: Art is hard. That’s why there’s an industry around it. The models aren’t ready. You have to get creative.

replies.author: Bluetails_Buizel
replies.body: Thankfully, there are free websites that teach you how to be good at it, like drawabox.com but I’m there just for advice, picking up the pencil is just a side quest.

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body:
The alternative is shift where you compromise - make the game, use AI assets as "good enough" to convey the style and vibe, and seek a publisher or try to revshare with an artist to replace the placeholders.

Depends on if your goal is to make money or make the best game you can align with your vision.

yep this is it.

replies.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
replies.body:
I am also doing VR development and found Claude to be very good at low poly. I have been using Astra+Blender and it has been pushing put 5000 poly assets (I am working on buildings atm). Gave the same instructions to Claude and it gave me a 600 poly model that looked just as good.

I have found Claude to be worse at making textures. It needs more hand-holding with the textures.

comments.author: Meretruth
comments.body: You have to get good at blender and get good at explaining what you need. Add steps that make Claude explain what it’s doing and what it could do instead, you start to slowly learn what to tell it to do and what to tell it not to do. If you know nothing Claude is blind leading the blind.

replies.author: IntelligentDot2924
replies.body: That wouldn’t be Claude. You’d need a model built for 3D generation. [fal.ai](http://fal.ai) offers models such as Hunyuan3D V3, and there are also local models that can run on a 6 GB GPU, though they require considerably more manual setup. Claude can help with the workflow, but you’d need MCP tools to connect everything. Expect to clean up the generated model in Blender before using it in a production project.

comments.author: uterhausen2002
comments.body:
I’m still learning as well, but I have instructed Claude to always research best practices before proposing a solution.   At one point it suggested that a prop would pull my character’s hands which is what caused me to do this.  It had also at one point tried to animate a skin rig directly and I had to do some research and make it build a control rig.

I’m still not even sure if I am still missing steps as I’m teaching myself, but tl;dr do research on how people do this without AI and use that framework at least to support your AI attempts.

comments.author: GT86
comments.body:
Still figuring it out but I've been trying a lot of different things. I have a little bit of experience in 3d graphics and blender. But gave never been that good at it. But I understand the tools enough to know what helps and what doesn't. 

What I'm narrowing down at the moment is. 

Chatgpt image gen to create reference. Having that creat orthogonal side front back bottom top references and a few perspective shots for context. 

Run the output through nano banana pro to ensure the orthogonal images do actually line up. 

Send that output to Claude to measure, confirm, resize and stretch if needed. 

Take that output. Run It through tripo on smart mesh from its orthogonal input, Max poly count do about 4 to 6 iterations. 

Get it to texture and apply pbr. 

From there the exported fbx Claude can work with it quite well to refine, break into parts, texture paint, etc as tripo actually produces quite a decent mesh. But Claude can fill the gaps. Find the holes. Ensure the normals are all in the right direction, cut and half and mirror for true symmetry and then run with it from there. 

Now mind you I'm only testing this on hard surface vehicles so far. Organise and characters this may not work. But it was a lot quicker and better than having Claude try do it from scratch on max in blender itself.
